framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request assumes rejected shipment notices can be auto-fixed and resubmitted by an AI agent, implying the root cause is correctable data errors in the notices rather than process or rule-alignment gaps between ORG-A and ORG-B.

hypotheses.statement: Rejected shipment notices (per DA-REJ) contain systematic, correctable data errors that an AI agent can detect and fix before resubmission, resolving carrier rejects.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-REQ's framing of the problem; if true it justifies building an auto-fix-and-resubmit agent as requested, but it has not been verified against the actual reject reasons in DA-REJ.
discriminating_evidence: Recurrence pattern of specific field-level errors across rejected notices

hypotheses.statement: Carrier rejects originate from ORG-B business validation rules (DA-REJ described as 'carrier business rejects') that ORG-A's shipment notice generation does not account for, rather than from random data entry mistakes.
hypotheses.rationale: If rejects are driven by business-rule mismatches rather than ad hoc errors, the fix is aligning rules/schemas between organizations, not a per-shipment auto-fix agent.
discriminating_evidence: DA-REJ reject reason codes categorized as business-rule violations vs data-entry errors
Comparison of ORG-B rule documentation (if any) against notice content standards

hypotheses.statement: The shipment notice process (P-1) lacks a mechanism to feed carrier reject information back into notice creation, so the same error types recur regardless of any downstream fix step.
hypotheses.rationale: If repeat rejects stem from an absent feedback loop in P-1 (whose pain_points/steps are currently empty/unknown), the solution is process redesign upstream rather than a reactive fix-and-resubmit bot.
discriminating_evidence: P-1 steps and pain_points once populated
Repeat-offender pattern of identical error types across time in DA-REJ

hypotheses.statement: The true causes of carrier rejects are not yet knowable because DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN, making any root-cause claim (including the auto-fix framing) premature.
hypotheses.rationale: DA-REJ's completeness field is explicitly UNKNOWN; if the log does not capture all reject reasons or categories, no hypothesis about root cause can be confirmed and building a solution now risks solving the wrong problem.
discriminating_evidence: DA-REJ completeness attribute and any audit of its field coverage
Cross-check of reject-log tool_id 'reject-log' output against known total reject volume

output.root_problem: Shipment notices generated by ORG-A's process P-1 are being rejected by ORG-B's carrier system because the notice generation logic does not account for ORG-B's carrier business validation rules, producing categorized rejects (2/3 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1/3 EVENT_ORDER per E-01) rather than random, undifferentiated carrier failures.
output.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them to the carrier.
symptoms: 3 shipment notices in the carrier reject log (DA-REJ) are rejected by ORG-B, with 2 tagged reason LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 tagged EVENT_ORDER (E-01, F-01, F-02).
causal_chain: ORG-A's shipment notice generation process (P-1) produces notices without accounting for ORG-B's carrier business validation rules (H-BUSINESS-RULE-GAP, supported by E-01).
These rule-mismatched notices fail carrier-side validation, generating categorized rejects: LOC_UNKNOWN in 2 of 3 records and EVENT_ORDER in 1 of 3 records (E-01, F-01, F-02).

Rejected notices accumulate in the carrier reject log (DA-REJ) without a correction mechanism addressing the specific validation gap, prompting the stakeholder request for an automated resubmission fix (CL-01).

assumptions.statement: The business-rule gap originates in ORG-A's notice generation step of P-1 rather than elsewhere in the H-1 handoff, since E-01 characterizes reject reasons but not the exact origin point.
The two observed reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) are stable, representative categories rather than artifacts of a tiny 3-record sample.

unknowns.resolution_path: Interview P-1 process owners / review process documentation for existing feedback mechanisms.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Implement the identified rule fixes now and separately evaluate whether a recurring feedback mechanism is needed.

output.summary: Problem (PD-1): ORG-A's P-1 shipment notices are rejected by ORG-B's carrier in categorized ways, not randomly. Of 3 sampled rejects (E-01, F-01, F-02), 2 were LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 was EVENT_ORDER. Stakeholder SH-REQ requested an AI auto-fix agent (CL-01) and framed the carrier as flaky (CL-02, E-02). Testing against E-01 rejected that framing (H-AUTO-FIX-VIABLE REJECTED) and supported H-BUSINESS-RULE-GAP, that P-1 does not account for ORG-B's validation rules. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring a critical completeness unknown to VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN. What was released is only the diagnostic rule-mapping step SR-RULE-MAPPING, satisfying SC-ROOT-CAUSE-MAPPED. The actual fix, redesigning P-1 logic, was infeasible in contest time and deferred. Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with an empty hold list, because open obligations VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN and VOB-R-2 block scopes outside what was released, so they did not force a hold but are carried as known limitations.
key_points: Root problem per PD-1: P-1 notice-generation logic does not account for ORG-B's carrier validation rules, producing categorized not random rejects, 2/3 LOC_UNKNOWN and 1/3 EVENT_ORDER (E-01, F-01, F-02).
SH-REQ's requested auto-fix solution (CL-01) and flaky-carrier framing (CL-02/E-02) were tested against E-01; H-AUTO-FIX-VIABLE was REJECTED and H-BUSINESS-RULE-GAP was SUPPORTED instead.
DEFINE gate for PD-1 returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical completeness unknown U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN into VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN rather than resolving it.

Released scope (SD-1): mapping carrier validation rules to P-1 fields via remedy SR-RULE-MAPPING, satisfying SC-ROOT-CAUSE-MAPPED; this remedy is explicitly diagnostic only (removes_root_cause=false).

Deferred and unreleased: redesigning P-1 notice-generation logic (SR-NOTICE-LOGIC-REDESIGN, removes_root_cause=true) is not feasible in contest time; feedback-loop remedy SR-FEEDBACK-LOOP and completeness-resolution remedy SR-COMPLETENESS-RESOLUTION also deferred.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, hold list empty; VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN and VOB-R-2 have blocking_scope outside the actual release scope, so they did not force a hold but remain open and are listed as limitations.
limitations_explained: The mapping analysis rests on a 3-record reject-log sample (DA-REJ) whose completeness is UNKNOWN (U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN, deferred to VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN); LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER proportions could differ at scale.
This release is diagnostic only; SR-RULE-MAPPING has removes_root_cause=false, so it identifies the mapping but does not by itself reduce the carrier reject rate.
Whether P-1 already has a feedback mechanism for carrier reject reasons is unconfirmed (U-FEEDBACK-LOOP-GAP / VOB-R-2, OPEN), so remedy SR-FEEDBACK-LOOP cannot yet be designed with certainty.
Whether genuine carrier-side system variability also contributes to rejects alongside the categorized rule mismatches is unconfirmed (U-CARRIER-SIDE-VARIABILITY, OPEN, LOW criticality).

The actual root-cause fix, redesigning P-1's notice-generation logic, is assessed as not feasible within contest time (SR-NOTICE-LOGIC-REDESIGN) and is deferred, so the reject rate is not expected to improve from this release alone.

Two verification obligations remain OPEN at release time: VOB-U-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN (HIGH impact, required BEFORE_RELEASE) and VOB-R-2 (MEDIUM impact, required BEFORE_DESIGN_FINALIZATION); both block scopes outside what was actually released.
